- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and prices are falling, model often underestimates drop; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for mean reversion.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 2–5% downward adjustment for first 7–10 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and history shows volatility, model tends to smooth out extremes; use 1–2% volatility buffer to reflect true range.  
- If sentiment spikes to 1.0 and model forecasts rise sharply, check for overfitting; reduce forecast by 5–10% if price correction is expected within 3–5 days.
